scope: AQA first school mock: Year 1/AS Pure only (no Statistics, Mechanics, Year 2)
notes: Six original multi-step AQA-style questions, not copied historic AQA paper questions. Mark points are worked illustrative methods, not AQA-issued official mark schemes.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: First-mock AS Pure challenge
questions.prompt: The integer n satisfies −3 ≤ n ≤ 3. Prove by exhaustion that n³ − n is divisible by 6 for every allowed n.
markPoints: List all seven integer cases n = −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3.
Every result is a multiple of 6, so the finite case list proves the claim.
questions.modelAnswer: List all seven integer cases n = −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. For n = −3, −2, −1, n³−n equals −24, −6, 0. For n = 0, 1, 2, 3, n³−n equals 0, 0, 6, 24. Every result is a multiple of 6, so the finite case list proves the claim.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: First-mock AS Pure challenge
questions.prompt: Find all solutions in degrees to 2sin²θ + cosθ − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ < 360°. Show each algebraic step.
markPoints: In the stated interval θ=0°, 120°, 240°, and no other solutions.
questions.modelAnswer: Use sin²θ=1−cos²θ to obtain 2(1−cos²θ)+cosθ−1=0. Rearrange to 2cos²θ−cosθ−1=0. Factorise as (2cosθ+1)(cosθ−1)=0. So cosθ=1 or cosθ=−1/2. In the stated interval θ=0°, 120°, 240°, and no other solutions.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: First-mock AS Pure challenge
questions.subtopic: Circles, completing the square, tangent gradient
questions.prompt: Circle C has equation x²+y²−6x+4y−12=0. Find its centre and radius. Verify P=(6,2) lies on C and find the equation of the tangent at P, in the form ax+by+c=0.
markPoints: At P, (6−3)²+(2+2)²=9+16=25, so P lies on C.
Gradient of the radius CP is 4/3, so the tangent gradient is −3/4.
questions.modelAnswer: Complete the square to (x−3)²+(y+2)²=25. Centre (3,−2), radius 5. At P, (6−3)²+(2+2)²=9+16=25, so P lies on C. Gradient of the radius CP is 4/3, so the tangent gradient is −3/4. The tangent is y−2=−3(x−6)/4, or 3x+4y−26=0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: First-mock AS Pure challenge
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=x²+2x−3 and g(x)=−2f(x−3)+1. Complete the square for f. Describe, in order, the graph transformations from y=f(x) to y=g(x). Find the turning point and exact x-intercepts of g.
questions.modelAnswer: Complete the square: f(x)=(x+1)²−4. Translate the graph 3 units right. Reflect in the x-axis. Stretch vertically by scale factor 2. Translate 1 unit up. g(x)=−2(x−2)²+9, with turning point (2,9). Set g(x)=0 to obtain x=2±3/√2 (equivalently 2±3√2/2).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: First-mock AS Pure challenge
questions.prompt: In the expansion of (2+ax)^5, the coefficient of x² is 720 and the coefficient of x³ is positive. Find the value of a and the coefficient of x⁴, showing your working.
markPoints: As the x³ coefficient is positive, a=3.
questions.modelAnswer: The x² coefficient is 10×2³×a² = 80a². 80a²=720, so a²=9 and a=±3. The x³ coefficient is 10×2²×a³ = 40a³. As the x³ coefficient is positive, a=3. The x⁴ coefficient is 5×2×a⁴ = 10×81 = 810.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: First-mock AS Pure challenge
questions.subtopic: Area with positive and negative sections
questions.prompt: The curve y=x²−4x+3 and the x-axis bound regions for 0≤x≤4. Calculate the total area between the curve and x-axis over this interval, taking care with sections below the axis.
markPoints: Factorise y=(x−1)(x−3), giving roots x=1 and x=3.
The area from x=0 to 1 is ∫₀¹y dx = 4/3.
From x=1 to 3 the integral is −4/3, so its area is 4/3.
The area from x=3 to 4 is ∫₃⁴y dx = 4/3.
Add the positive areas: total area = 4 square units.
questions.modelAnswer: Factorise y=(x−1)(x−3), giving roots x=1 and x=3. An antiderivative is F(x)=x³/3−2x²+3x. The area from x=0 to 1 is ∫₀¹y dx = 4/3. From x=1 to 3 the integral is −4/3, so its area is 4/3. The area from x=3 to 4 is ∫₃⁴y dx = 4/3. Add the positive areas: total area = 4 square units.
